quarterly_data.signal: Cisco's 10-K: inventory purchase commitments with contract manufacturers and suppliers were $17,165 million at July 25, 2026 versus $7,599 million at July 26, 2025 (up 126%), inventories were $5,694 million versus $3,164 million (up 80%), and inventory deposits and prepayments were $1,104 million versus $825 million, principally under arrangements to secure supply and pricing for memory and certain components. Cisco attributes the increase primarily to commitments related to manufacturing Cisco Silicon One and other products to meet demand from hyperscalers and other customers, with higher memory prices and commitments to secure memory supply also contributing significantly; some commitments are long-term supply agreements for fixed quantities of memory components at variable prices, and Cisco cites the memory shortages experienced in fiscal 2026. Of the purchase commitments, $14,341 million are due in less than one year.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory purchase commitments $17,165 million (+126%); inventories $5,694 million (+80%); inventory deposits and prepayments $1,104 million vs $825 million

quarterly_data.signal: Cisco's 10-K: total remaining performance obligations were $46,734 million at the end of fiscal 2026 versus $43,533 million at the end of fiscal 2025, up 7%, with product RPO up 9% and services RPO up 6%. Cisco expects to recognize approximately 49% of total RPO as revenue over the next 12 months, approximately 39% between one and three years and approximately 12% thereafter.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $46,734 million vs $43,533 million (+7%); product RPO +9%; ~49% to be recognized within 12 months
